messages:
tara: Quick sync — we need a final runbook for the Elysian silicon preview. They asked for a single, actionable doc we can hand to their lab tomorrow. Must include NDA confirmation, bench scripts, telemetry hooks, and a 48h feedback loop.

jake: I'll draft the bench checklist. Curious which SLOs we publicly commit to for the preview — p95/p99, and token/sec targets?

maria: From the email thread: partner-facing promise is p99 < 120ms for 8k context. Internally we should capture token/sec, cost-per-token, and cold-start latency.

tara: Correct — p99 < 120ms is the external number. Add cold-start and first-token latency to the metrics list.

elysian-eng: (partner) Lab access confirmed at 10:00 PT tomorrow. NDA signed (DocuSign: https://docusign.example/elysian). Can we include exact docker image and kernel flags in the runbook?

samir: Will add kernel flags and the recommended image. Example run:```bash
docker run --gpus all -e REDWOOD_ENV=preview \
  -v /mnt/models:/models \
  redwood/inference:preview-quant-v2 \
  --kernels=warp-attn,kv-cache-opt --max-seq=8192
```

samir: Perf script we'll run: `scripts/bench/throughput.sh --context 8192 --batch 4 --duration 300`. Include warmup cycles (5 mins) before measurement.

jake: Bench checklist sections: prereqs, run order (baseline → quant → kv-cache), data collection (latency distribution, tokens/s, mem, gpu_util, syscalls), artifact tagging, and plotting commands.

olivia: On telemetry: we need a minimal, anonymized payload back to Redwood. Elysian asked for raw logs for debug but Legal warned about proprietary data leakage.

legal-bot: Legal note: partner logs may contain proprietary/PII. Get explicit consent and run redaction prior to transfer. Use: `tools/redact/strip-pii.py`. If partner insists on raw logs, use S3 with limited retention and KMS.

maria: We'll request perf counters only. If they require low-level logs, use the S3 + KMS flow and redact PII. Document retention TTL (7 days) and access list.

tara: Feedback loop: daily standups (first 3 days, 30m) then async. All issues go into `rwd/elysian-preview` GitHub repo. Who can create the repo + templates?

jake: I'll create the repo and add an issue template with categories: `bug`, `regression`, `tuning-suggestion`. I'll also add a triage checklist.

elysian-eng: Can we wire automated alerts for regressions tied to telemetry thresholds? We'll want threshold docs in the runbook.

samir: Proposed thresholds: token/s drop >10% = alert; p99 >120ms = P0; GPU mem >85% = investigate. I'll add exact Grafana queries and example alert payloads.

olivia: Define on-call ownership for the preview: primary, backup, and escalation path. Also include Slack huddle link for quick calls.

tara: Primary: maria. Backup: jake. Escalate to infra-oncall if both unavailable. I'll add phone numbers and the huddle link.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled deployment to preview namespace at 09:30 PT tomorrow. Image: redwood/inference:preview-quant-v2.

jake: Also add dependency matrix: supported CUDA + driver versions, required kernel modules, and known firmware compatibility notes. Partner lab has mixed firmware, so compatibility guidance is important.

elysian-eng: We'll share firmware list. We also have a memcpy perf patch for the new boards — can you run A/B tests with and without?

maria: Add an A/B step: run identical bench flows on stock firmware (v1) and patched firmware (v1-patch). Tag artifacts with `firmware=stock` or `firmware=patch`.

tara: I'll assemble the runbook and share a read-only Drive link once it's ready. Jake/Samir/Olivia, please review the draft in #partnerships today.

jake: Aiming to push the draft by 16:00 PT.

maria: Will prepare the redaction + S3 retention policy snippet.

elysian-eng: Thanks — excited to kick this off. See you at 10:00 PT tomorrow. :rocket:

tara: Thanks team :thumbsup:
